#### Suggested Prompts

An answer can hand back a prompt for the user to send, as a fenced code block whose info string is `suspense-prompt`, followed by a space and the mode it is meant for, `code`, `chain`, `spec`, `ask`, or `freeform`, as the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) names them, and holding the prompt's text, as the card format of the [ModeSystemPromptsScope](../mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts-scope) tells the harness. Such a block is never shown as a code block. It is shown in the answer, where it stands among the reply's markdown, as a prompt card: a box on the theme's raised surface, faintly tinted the mode's colour, with corners rounded 6 pixels, across the answer's full width. Along its top runs a small header, the mode's icon and name in the mode's colour, as "Code prompt", and beneath it the prompt's text as it was written, wrapped, in the body's text colour, not rendered as markdown.
A card starts collapsed, its text cut to its first line, cut off with an ellipsis, and a chevron at the right of its header. Clicking the header or the chevron expands it to show the whole prompt, the chevron turning down, and clicking again collapses it; its buttons work either way, sending or copying the whole prompt. Each card stays as it was left for as long as the application runs, and expanding or collapsing one never scrolls the pane. Along its bottom, at its right, is a row of small buttons, 4 pixels apart, wrapping onto another line where the card is too

##### Narrow

Copy, with a copy icon, which puts the prompt's text on the

clipboard; Edit, with a pencil icon, as below; and then "Send to Code", "Send to Chain", and "Send to Spec", in that order, each with an arrow icon and in its mode's colour, as the [PromptModesScope](../modes/index.md#prompt-modes-scope) colours them. The send button for the card's own mode, where it is one of those three, is filled in its colour, and the others are ghost buttons in theirs, so the one the answer meant stands out while every task mode is a click away. A card for `ask` or `freeform` has, before the three, "Ask" or "Send to Freeform", filled in that mode's colour, the three after it as ghosts.
Each send button sends the prompt's text at once, in its mode, as though it had been written in the [ChatInputScope](../chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) on that tab and sent, as the [PromptSendingScope](../sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) says, the Chain button sending it as a Chain prompt: a task is compiled anew, building the spec first, and queues while its lane is busy, and a question runs at once. It is sent with the Slice toggle as it stands, with nothing attached, and what is being written in the chat input, and attached to it, is left alone. The button then reads "Sent to Code", "Sent to Chain", "Sent to Spec", "Asked", or "Sent to Freeform", with a check, and keeps reading so: it never times out or resets, and it is disabled for good, so the prompt is never sent twice from it, however long after, and across restarts, kept with the question's record. The card's other send buttons stay as they were, so the prompt can still be sent to another mode, each once. The tooltip of each says what it does, as "Send this prompt as a Code task".
Edit puts the prompt's text in the chat input's text input instead, and selects the card's mode's tab, Chain for Code and Spec selected together where the mode is `chain`, giving the input keyboard focus with the cursor at the end of the text. It never sends anything: the user reads, edits, and sends it as any prompt. Where the input already holds text, that text is set aside first as the chat input sets aside a prompt for editing a queued one, and comes back once the prompt from the card is sent or cleared, so nothing typed is lost. What is attached to the prompt being written stays attached. The button reads "Edited", with a check, for 2 seconds after.
A block whose mode is missing or isn't one of those five is still a prompt card, headed "Prompt", in Ask's colour, with all three send buttons as ghosts, and Edit selects Chain, the tab the chat input starts on. While a block is still streaming in, its card is shown with what has come so far and its buttons disabled until the block closes. A block never closed by the end of a finished answer is a card all the same, holding what came. An answer may hold any number of cards, each in its place.

#### Scrolling

The pane scrolls, with a [ScrollbarScope](../../../ui/components/scrollbar/index.md#scrollbar-scope), and opens scrolled to the bottom, on the newest question, the first time it is shown. While it is at the bottom it stays locked there, following each question asked and each answer as it grows; scrolling up unlocks it, and scrolling back to the bottom locks it again. Asking a question always scrolls it to the bottom and locks it. When a question's answer finishes, however it ended, the pane scrolls so the start of that answer is at its top, unlocking it, so the answer is read from its beginning, unless the user scrolled the pane while it was answering, or another question is still answering beneath it, when it is left where it is. However many questions it holds, and however long their answers, it lays out only what is in view: each question, divider, summary line, and block of an answer's markdown is drawn as it scrolls into view, so a long conversation costs no more to show, scroll, or resize than a short one.

Prompt cards in Ask answers now start collapsed, send buttons stay "Sent to X" for good, and a finished answer is scrolled to its start. On the full run 554 tests passed and one failed: `quitting_while_a_task_runs_asks_first`, a test that has been flaky before. It passed three times on its own, and clippy has nothing new in `ask_pane.rs`.

- **Collapsed cards:** each card shows only its first line, with an ellipsis if there's more. Clicking the header or its chevron expands or collapses it without scrolling the pane. The state lasts while the app runs, and the buttons always send or copy the whole prompt.
- **Sent buttons:** once clicked, a send button keeps its check and "Sent to X" label and is disabled for good. That's saved in the question's record, so it holds across restarts. The card's other send buttons still work, once each, and only Edit's "Edited" still clears after 2 seconds.
- **Scrolling:** when an answer finishes, including when it's stopped, the pane scrolls so the answer's start is at the top. It doesn't if you scrolled since the question was asked, or if a question below it is still answering. Freeform chats, which share this pane code, don't do this; the spec only asks it of the Ask pane.

The spec and your prompt agree.
